clue.text: It is profoundly offensive in the main

definitions.text: It is profoundly offensive in the main

parts.words: It is profoundly offensive in the main
parts.note: read as a weapon that attacks at great depth out on the open sea, 'the main' being an old word for the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'Profoundly' means at great depth and 'offensive' is a military attack, while 'the main' is the sea, not 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: This weapon is an anti-submarine charge set to explode deep underwater.

clue.text: A moving study?

parts.note: read not as an emotional piece of research but as the branch of science that studies motion and the forces causing it

explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' suggests touching or emotional; here it means about motion.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of mechanics deals with bodies in motion and the forces acting on them.

clue.text: Place in which Greek character's found botanical specimen

indicators.note: in which says the Greek letter sits inside the abbreviation for place
found completes the sense that the letter is located within the place

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person is discovered somewhere holding a plant sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person but is a letter of the Greek alphabet; 'in which ... found' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured parts of a flower, a botanical item.

clue.text: Keeps taking one's drug? Wait for it

parts.note: to keep something is to hold it
one's means your, as in 'your own'
horse is a slang name for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on taking their drug, and is told to be patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin; 'taking' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an idiom urging someone to be patient and not rush ahead.

clue.text: Eye, say, last and first letters in flimsy stuff

parts.note: an eye is an example of an organ of the body
the last and first letters of the alphabet are Z and A

explanation.surface: An eye and some letters appear printed on delicate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last and first letters' means of the alphabet, giving Z then A, not letters of a clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, sheer fabric made of silk or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Oils hob to cook for Russian ballet

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it over, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Grease the stove to make dinner for the Moscow dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cook' rearranges OILS HOB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshoi is Moscow's famous ballet company and theatre.

clue.text: Vibrating sound we heard in rotor initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Someone describes the buzzing they heard coming from a spinning rotor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'we heard in rotor'; 'heard' looks like a sound-alike signal but is only one of the words picked from.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirring noise is the steady hum of something spinning or vibrating fast.

clue.text: Oils hob to cook for Rabble from Hungary with two exclamations about vote

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Oils hob to cook for Rabble from Hungary with two exclamations about vote (3,6)' carries the words of 5-down on this light too; the real clue would be 'Rabble from Hungary with two exclamations about vote', but no print confirms it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Oils hob to cook for Rabble from Hungary with two exclamations about vote

clue.text: Very indirect about any tiny thing

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a mote is a speck, as of dust

explanation.surface: Someone is very roundabout about any small matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote can mean distant or slight, far removed from the direct line.

clue.text: Role conviction played in musical work

indicators.note: played suggests an actor performing, but signals these letters being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor plays a role with conviction in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges ROLE CONVICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a piece for solo instrument and orchestra, here featuring the fiddle.

clue.text: Some function at a locus of origin

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mathematician talks about the value of a function at a particular locus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'functioN AT A Locus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal describes things connected with birth, the point where a person's life begins.

clue.text: Source of bitterness to multinational backing manuscript? That's what the French say

parts.note: gall is bile, and figuratively bitterness or resentment
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a large British multinational company

indicators.note: backing has the abbreviation for manuscript turned round to run the other way

explanation.surface: A big company's resentment towards a manuscript prompts a French remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns MS into SM. ICI was the British chemicals giant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gallicism is an idiom or turn of phrase borrowed from French.

clue.text: Chap accepting a bet relating to eastern peninsula

indicators.note: accepting means the word for a chap takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man
to lay is to bet, as in laying odds

explanation.surface: A man agrees to take a wager about somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the container; 'bet' is a verb sense, to lay odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaya is the peninsula of South-East Asia, so the adjective describes it or its people.

clue.text: Don't give in to cargo storage that's unfashionable

parts.note: the hold is the part of a ship where cargo is stowed
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to yield over an outdated ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out is to resist and refuse to surrender or concede.

clue.text: Not a single sex lesson taught in this school?

definitions.text: Not a single sex lesson taught in this school?

parts.words: Not a single sex lesson taught in this school?
parts.note: sounds like a school banning sex education, but means a school that is not single-sex, teaching boys and girls together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a single sex lesson' reads as no sex education at all; split it as 'not a single-sex' school.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed school teaches pupils of both genders in the same classes.

clue.text: Smooth bread as likely as not

parts.note: even means level or smooth
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Plain bread is as good a bet as any.
explanation.definitionFit: These are betting odds where the stake equals the possible win, a fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: Staggered at thyme's growing in stone

indicators.note: staggered means reeling about, so these letters lurch into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at how well thyme grows among rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' looks like 'amazed' but rearranges AT THYMES; 'growing in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An amethyst is a violet variety of quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Showing inclination?

parts.note: read as a tendency or urge to show off, to put oneself on display, rather than revealing a preference

explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing inclination' sounds like displaying a preference; read it as an inclination for showing oneself off.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a compulsion to attract attention by extravagant behaviour or by exposing oneself.

clue.text: With little material to wrap fish it'll show the price

indicators.note: to wrap means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: bare means with few clothes on, so with little material
cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: A fish is wrapped in skimpy material to be priced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With little material' reads as a phrase about scanty cloth but gives a single adjective; 'to wrap' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped code scanned at a till identifies an item and its price.

clue.text: Movement of train's upset before junction

indicators.note: before means the rearranged letters come ahead of the next piece
upset as of an overturned train, here meaning the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a T-junction, so T can stand for a junction

explanation.surface: A train comes off the rails just ahead of a junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes TRANSI; 'before' puts that ahead of the junction letter. A T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage or conveyance from one place to another.

clue.text: Involved in delay, paid nothing for pet

indicators.note: involved in means the next pieces are taken into the word for delay

parts.note: a lag is a delay
PD is the abbreviation for paid, as on a receipt
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a hold-up got their pet for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved in' signals the container; 'paid' is cut to its receipt abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered dog kept as a companion.

clue.text: Worshipper married in unorthodox setting

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Worshipper married in unorthodox setting (7)': M (married) inside ADIRER needs anagram fodder such as RAIDER, which no word of the held clue supplies; the clue appears cut or garbled by OCR.

clue.text: Old canine teeth initially decayed

indicators.note: decayed suggests rotten teeth, but signals that the letters break down and reform
initially takes just the opening letter of the word teeth

explanation.surface: An elderly dog's teeth have started to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decayed' rearranges CANINE to ANCIEN, and 'initially' adds T from 'teeth'; the surface makes it read as rotten dog's teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, belonging to a long-past age.

clue.text: Wear down with hesitation starting poem

indicators.note: starting puts the hesitation sound at the beginning of the word for poem

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poet hesitates before beginning to recite, worn down.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water does to rock.

clue.text: Party from America accepting incense is unsafe

indicators.note: accepting means the party and America together take another word inside

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
to incense is to anger, used here as a verb

explanation.surface: An American celebration that admits burning incense is a fire risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' looks like the fragrant stuff but is the verb, to enrage; 'accepting' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous means likely to cause harm, the opposite of safe.

clue.text: Large dock seen from behind yard

indicators.note: seen from behind means the word for dock is read from its back end forwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

explanation.surface: A big dock and yard viewed from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen from behind' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, with plenty of space inside.

clue.text: Painter unknown in part of India

indicators.note: in places the unknown letter inside the name of the Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Y can stand for one

explanation.surface: An unknown artist turns up in an Indian region.
explanation.walkthrough: Algebra's unknowns x, y, z give Y here.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish artist of the late 1700s and early 1800s.

clue.text: Unusual text about pirate with outgoing personality

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the pirate
Unusual says the letters of text appear in a strange new order

parts.note: a rover is an old word for a pirate or sea-robber

explanation.surface: A strange piece of writing about a pirate with a lively character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' makes EXTT, and 'about' wraps it round the old word for a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sociable and confident who enjoys company is the opposite of an introvert.
